title: Fishhawk upkeep report artifact (plan-stage sibling)
description: The THIRD additive sibling of the plan artifact (after clarification-request-v1 and grooming-report-v1), produced by a `plan`-typed PROPOSE stage that DECLARES `produces: upkeep_report` (E79 / #3726, #3921). Selected over plan-standard-v1 by the top-level 'kind' discriminator BEFORE validation, so plan-standard-v1.schema.json stays frozen. An upkeep report is a PROPOSAL, never an applied mutation: it lists the maintenance findings a scan found (flaky tests, toolchain drift, deprecations, vulnerability advisories), each with the evidence that supports it and the issue it proposes filing, and a human decides what (if anything) to file. `sources_scanned` records what the scan COVERED, so an empty `findings` array reads 'none found', not 'not scanned'. Every finding carries a stable `id` DERIVED as `<source>:<subject>` (never minted per run), so two reports over the same tree diff mechanically and a filed issue's hidden marker `<!-- fishhawk-upkeep:v1 finding_id=<id> -->` matches exactly. Cross-field rules the schema cannot state (id derivation, uniqueness, run-id syntax, per-source evidence shape, label syntax, and the advisory rules: reachability derived from the call path, severity capped by reachability, scanner/ecosystem pairing, a cited manifest, a bare fixed version, source_degrades consistency and the advisory source accounted for) are enforced by the backend semantic layer; see upkeep-report-v1.md for the normative contract.

kind.description: Top-level discriminator. The plan package routes an artifact carrying this value to this schema. This sibling intentionally omits plan_version so the artifacts never collide on a shared required field.

report_version.description: Artifact schema version. Single-value enum: a future breaking change bumps to upkeep_report_v2 with its own schema file rather than editing this one in place.

summary.description: Human-readable lead paragraph: what the scan covered and the headline of what it proposes. Rendered first at the operator gate.

sources_scanned.description: The detector sources this scan RAN. Every finding's `source` must appear here (a semantic rule). Recording coverage separately from findings is what lets an empty `findings` array mean 'scanned, none found' rather than 'not scanned'. A source the scan could not run is left OUT of this array and named in `source_degrades` instead.

findings.description: The findings, each proposing one issue. May be empty. Capped at 200 so one report bounds the ingest's dedupe and run-ref lookups.

source_degrades.description: Optional (#3750). The NAMED degradations of this scan: one entry per source that could not run at all (reason other than `partial`; the source is then NOT in sources_scanned) or that ran only in part (reason `partial`; the source IS in sources_scanned). It is what keeps an advisory scan that could not reach its database from reading as a clean 'none found'. At most one entry per source, and the reason/sources_scanned pairing, are semantic rules; so is the advisory accounting: a report carrying any entry here must list `advisory` in sources_scanned (it ran) or name it here with a reason other than `partial` (it did not run). The residual: a report with no entry here and no advisory finding cannot be told apart from a pre-#3750 report, so zero advisory findings from a scan that never ran advisories is not detectable.

ticket-reference.description: The ticket the grooming RUN was opened against (the run's originating issue), not an item being groomed. Shape mirrors plan-standard-v1 verbatim.

type.description: v0 closed set; v0.x adds linear_ticket and jira_ticket. Mirrors plan-standard-v1.

url.description: Canonical URL of the originating ticket.

agent.description: Agent identifier matching the workflow spec's executor.agent.

version.description: Optional. Model version or build SHA when agent reports it.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of generation. The runner wall-clock at agent invocation.

source.description: Detector source. flake: a test that failed and then passed on the same tree across runs. toolchain_drift: one tool pinned to different versions in different files. deprecation: use of a deprecated API or construct. advisory (#3750): a dependency the repository pins is named by a published vulnerability advisory; the finding carries an `advisory` object.

id.description: Stable finding id, DERIVED as `<source>:<subject>` (the backend checks the derivation and report-wide uniqueness). The pattern forbids whitespace and angle brackets so the hidden marker `<!-- fishhawk-upkeep:v1 finding_id=<id> -->` a filed issue carries matches EXACTLY: `flake:TestA` never matches the marker of `flake:TestAB`.

subject.description: What the finding is about, with no whitespace or angle bracket: a test name for flake, a tool name for toolchain_drift, an API or construct for deprecation, `<primary advisory id>:<package>` for advisory (a semantic rule). It is the id's suffix.

evidence.description: At least one evidence ref. The per-source shape (a flake cites a run; a toolchain_drift names at least two distinct lined file paths; a deprecation names a file; an advisory names at least one manifest file — basename go.mod, pnpm-lock.yaml or package.json) is a semantic rule.

evidence-ref.description: One evidence pointer, discriminated by `kind`: a run ref or a file ref.

run-evidence.description: A Fishhawk run that exhibits the finding. ONLY `run_id` is verified on ingest (it must name an existing run in the reporting run's repository); `stage_id` and `trace_ref` are AGENT-ASSERTED pointers the server never resolves.

run_id.description: The cited run's UUID. The backend requires a non-nil UUID naming a run in the same repository (and account, when both carry one).

stage_id.description: Optional stage UUID within the cited run. Agent-asserted: parsed as a UUID, never checked against the run.

trace_ref.description: Optional pointer into the cited stage's trace. Agent-asserted and unresolved.

detail.description: Optional free-text note on what this run shows.

file-evidence.description: A repository file that exhibits the finding.

value.description: Optional value found at path:line (e.g. the pinned version string).

proposed-issue.description: The issue the finding proposes filing. Filing is a separate, gated step (#3924); an open issue already carrying this finding's marker, or a similar title, marks the finding a duplicate at ingest instead. For an `advisory` finding the filed title and body are SERVER-RENDERED from the advisory object, so the agent-authored title and body here are read at the gate but never reach the tracker (#3750).

body.description: Proposed issue body. The apply step appends the hidden finding marker; the agent need not include it.

labels.description: Proposed label names; may be empty. Each must pass the label syntax rule (a semantic rule). An `autonomy:*` label is STRIPPED at apply unless the captain authorizes it (#3924): the scan may suggest a tier, never set one.

parent_epic.description: Optional parent epic: a positive issue number, bare or `#`-prefixed (a semantic rule).

advisory.description: The advisory facts of an `advisory` finding (#3750). Present on, and only on, a finding whose source is `advisory` (a semantic rule). The scan agent copies these from the scanner output; the server cannot re-run the scanner, so it BOUNDS the claim instead: `reachability` must equal the level derived from `call_path[0]`, `severity` is capped by `reachability`, `scanner` pairs with `ecosystem`, and the finding must cite a manifest file. Normative contract: upkeep-report-v1.md.

ecosystem.description: Package ecosystem of the affected dependency.

package.description: The affected dependency. For Go this is the MODULE path (golang.org/x/net), never the vulnerable package path inside it (golang.org/x/net/http2); for npm, the package name. It is the subject's suffix after the primary advisory id.

version.description: The in-use version. When one finding cites several manifests, the LOWEST in-use version across them.

advisory_ids.description: Advisory identifiers. Index 0 is the PRIMARY id the subject is derived from: the GO- id for Go, the GHSA id for npm. Aliases (CVE, GHSA) follow.

fixed_version.description: ONE bare version carrying the fix (the lowest patched version on the in-use major line), or an explicit null when the advisory has no fix. Never a range: a value carrying any of `<>=^~|*`, whitespace or a comma is refused (a semantic rule). REQUIRED: absence is a schema error, so 'no fix' is always stated, never implied.

scanner.description: The scanner that reported the advisory. govulncheck pairs with go, pnpm_audit with npm, osv with either (a semantic rule). `osv` is RESERVED: no OSV command is instructed yet.

reachability.description: How deeply the repository reaches the vulnerable code. For govulncheck it must equal the level derived from call_path[0]: a function -> called, else a package -> imported, else a module -> required. pnpm_audit and osv report no reachability, so they are always unanalyzed.

call_path.description: govulncheck only, required non-empty there and absent or empty otherwise: the finding's `trace` copied VERBATIM from `govulncheck -json`, ordered from the vulnerable end (index 0) toward the entry point. A trace longer than 32 frames keeps index 0 onward and truncates the FAR end, never the vulnerable end.

severity.description: Proposed severity, CAPPED by reachability (a semantic rule): called may be any; imported and required at most low; unanalyzed at most medium.

advisory-frame.description: One govulncheck `-json` trace frame, with govulncheck's own field names (golang.org/x/vuln internal/govulncheck Frame), so a frame is copied verbatim. additionalProperties is false so a frame carrying an unexpected key is refused, not silently dropped.

module.description: Module path of the module containing the symbol; `stdlib` for the standard library.

version.description: Module version from the build graph.

receiver.description: Receiver type when the symbol is a method.

advisory-position.description: A govulncheck source position. The filename is relative to the enclosing module's directory and uses `/`.

line.description: Line, from 1 (0 marks an invalid position).

source-degrade.description: One named degradation of a source (#3750).

reason.description: network_unavailable: the source's database or registry was unreachable. tool_unavailable: the scanner is not installed and its fallback could not run. tool_failed: the scanner ran and failed. budget_exceeded: the stage ran out of time before the source finished. partial: the source ran, but not over everything (the detail names what was missed); only partial pairs with the source being in sources_scanned.

detail.description: Optional free-text: what failed or what was missed.
